headline_contributions: 1. First multi-label CXR classifier aligned with 51 Indonesian canonical labels from PDPI/PNPK/KKI clinical authority
2. Differentiable double-ReLU hierarchical penalty (vs. Asadi 2025 hard indicator — fully differentiable during training)
3. MC-Dropout variance gate for INFERENCE-TIME hierarchical fallback (vs. Pham 2020 training-time conditional data filtering)
4. AURC-based selective prediction evaluation using Zhou et al. (2025) plug-in estimator — novel metric for clinical CXR deployment

sections.title: Introduction
sections.purpose: CXR clinical motivation → multi-label challenge → hierarchy gap → uncertainty gap → contributions → paper road map
sections.structural_lesson_source: Pham 2020 intro structure (gap identification before contributions), Zhou 2025 (explicit contribution list)

key_claims: CXR: most common radiological exam; widespread in Indonesia but specialist-scarce
Automated multi-label classification can assist triage and screening
51 clinically relevant thoracic findings from Indonesian guidelines (PDPI/PNPK/KKI)
Multi-label: most CXRs show co-occurring findings — not single-disease classification

subsections.role: Gap 1 — flat classifiers ignore disease hierarchy
key_claims: Standard multi-label classifiers predict each finding independently
Clinical knowledge encodes IS-A relationships: Pneumonia implies Consolidation; COVID-19 Pneumonia implies Pneumonia
Flat classifiers produce hierarchically inconsistent outputs (child positive, parent negative) — clinically invalid
Prior work (Asadi 2025, Pham 2020) addresses hierarchy at TRAINING TIME: data filtering or loss penalty
Gap: no prior work applies hierarchy at INFERENCE TIME via uncertainty routing

subsections.role: Gap 2 — uncertainty is quantified but not used for decision routing
key_claims: Deep networks are overconfident — sigmoid output ≠ calibrated probability
MC-Dropout (Gal & Ghahramani 2016) estimates per-finding uncertainty via T stochastic passes
Prior hierarchical CXR methods produce no per-finding uncertainty signal at inference
Gap: when model is uncertain about a specific child finding, safer prediction is its parent — no method uses this routing
1. First multi-label CXR classifier targeting 51 Indonesian canonical labels (PDPI/PNPK/KKI), pooling 6 heterogeneous public datasets
2. Differentiable double-ReLU hierarchical penalty (HBCE): penalty(g,c) = ReLU(p_c−0.5)·ReLU(0.5−p_g) — fully differentiable alternative to Asadi 2025 hard indicator
3. Uncertainty-Gated Coarse Fallback: MC-Dropout variance gate at INFERENCE TIME — if σ_c > τ_u, suppress child, fall back to parent; no architecture change required
4. AURC-based selective prediction evaluation (Zhou 2025 plug-in estimator) — new metric for clinical deployment safety, comparing fallback model vs. flat baseline at matched coverage

sections.title: Related Work
sections.purpose: Cover: (a) hierarchical multi-label CXR, (b) uncertainty estimation for CXR, (c) selective prediction metrics
sections.structural_lesson_source: Pham 2020 (group by topic, not chronology); Asadi 2025 (compact, tight citations)

subsections.title: Hierarchical Multi-Label CXR Classification
key_claims: CheXpert (Irvin et al. 2019) [21] established 14-label hierarchy with uncertain labels; Pham 2020 exploited it via conditional training
Pham 2020: two-phase conditional training (parent-positive subset → finetune on full data); Bayes product at inference for p(child) ≤ p(parent)
Asadi 2025 (CIHMLC): HBCE loss with IS-A hard indicator penalty; MC-Dropout at inference but no uncertainty-based routing
Chen et al. 2019 (MIDL): hierarchical multi-label classification of CXR — conditional training on PLCO hierarchy
OUR DISTINCTION from Pham 2020: we apply hierarchy at INFERENCE TIME via variance gate, not training-time data filtering
OUR DISTINCTION from Asadi 2025: (a) differentiable ReLU penalty vs. hard indicator; (b) variance gate suppresses child when uncertain; (c) 51 Indonesian labels vs. 5-15 CheXpert labels

subsections.title: Uncertainty Estimation in Medical Imaging
key_claims: MC-Dropout (Gal & Ghahramani 2016): dropout at inference + T forward passes → mean + variance; Bayesian approximation
Deep ensembles (Lakshminarayanan 2017): multiple networks — effective but costly (we use single backbone)
ECE (Guo 2017): calibration measure; reliability diagrams for verification
Prior CXR uncertainty: Dvijotham 2023 (Nature Medicine) — complementarity-driven deferral to clinicians — related but single-label
OUR DISTINCTION: we use MC-Dropout variance as a per-LABEL gating signal, not just a rejection score for the whole image

subsections.title: Selective Prediction and AURC
key_claims: Selective classifiers abstain when uncertain (Chow 1970 original reject option concept)
AURC metric characterizes risk-coverage trade-off
Zhou et al. 2025 (ICML): formal population AURC + O(√ln(n)/n) plug-in estimator — safe citation (KU Leuven)
Franc et al. 2023 (JMLR): SELE score as AURC lower bound — shown to be unreliable by Zhou 2025
OUR NOVELTY: first application of AURC to hierarchical multi-label CXR selective prediction comparing fallback model vs. flat baseline

sections.purpose: Complete method description: problem → datasets → hierarchy → backbone → loss → uncertainty → gate → evaluation

subsections.title: Problem Formulation
key_claims: Multi-label classification: for image x, predict p ∈ [0,1]^51 (probability that each finding is present)
51 canonical findings from Indonesian clinical guidelines (PDPI/PNPK/KKI)
Label values y_c ∈ {0, 1, NaN}: 0=negative, 1=positive, NaN=not annotated by that dataset
NaN → applicability mask m_c=0: excluded from loss and metrics (never treated as confirmed negative)
IS-A relationships: for parent g with child set L(g), presence of any child c ∈ L(g) implies presence of parent g
Model may report at child level, fall back to parent, or abstain — depending on estimated uncertainty

notation_table.(g,c): IS-A edge: g = parent, c = child
notation_table.L(g): set of children of parent g

subsections.title: Datasets and Preprocessing
subsections.IMPORTANT_FIX: The current draft (Section B) lists PadChest, Open-I, RSNA as fine-tuning datasets — this is WRONG. These are in the TorchXRayVision backbone pretraining. Our ACTUAL fine-tuning datasets are listed below. Fix before submission.
actual_finetuning_datasets: NIH ChestX-ray14 (Wang et al. 2017): 112,120 frontal CXRs, 14 labels
CheXpert (Irvin et al. 2019): 224,316 frontal CXRs, 14 labels, uncertain annotations
VinDr-CXR (Nguyen et al. 2022): 18,000 CXRs, 28 pathologies, Vietnamese population
VinDr-PCXR (Pham et al. 2022): pediatric CXRs from Vietnam
TBX11K (Liu et al. 2020): 11,200 CXRs, TB-focused, bounding box annotations
subsections.backbone_pretraining_separate: TorchXRayVision densenet121-res224-all pretrained on NIH+PadChest+CheXpert+MIMIC-CXR+Open-I+RSNA — these are BACKBONE datasets, not our fine-tuning data
key_claims: All 6 datasets mapped to shared 51-label canonical set (src/data/label_space.py CANONICAL_LABELS)
Labels not annotated by a dataset → NaN → mask m_c=0 → excluded from loss and metrics
Single frontal image per study: PA > AP > other frontal (view priority)
Grayscale, TorchXRayVision pixel range [-1024, 1024]
Resize shorter side to 256 (bicubic), center crop to 224×224
DICOM: slope+intercept rescale, MONOCHROME1 invert, clip 0.5th–99.5th percentile before scaling
Uncertain labels (CheXpert -1): mapped to 0 (U-Zero convention) — different from Pham 2020's LSR
Augmentation (train only): affine ±10°, translate ±5%, scale [0.95,1.05], brightness/contrast ±0.1
Horizontal flipping DISABLED: mirrors cardiac silhouette (situs inversus anatomy would be wrongly flipped)
Patient-level splits: each source dataset's official split used; no patient in >1 partition
subsections.writing_note: State explicitly that the 51 canonical labels and 13 IS-A edges are NOT an official taxonomy — they are from Indonesian clinical guidelines (PDPI/PNPK/KKI) and clinically grounded IS-A relationships. The hierarchy file is external, allowing different edge sets without code changes.

subsections.title: Backbone and Classification Head
key_claims: DenseNet-121 (TorchXRayVision, weights densenet121-res224-all): pretrained on large heterogeneous CXR corpus
Two justifications: (1) domain-specific feature detectors unavailable in ImageNet-pretrained models; (2) convolutional features amenable to Grad-CAM localization
Backbone produces 1024-dim pooled feature vector
Single linear head: 1024→51 logits + per-finding sigmoid
Dropout layer (p=0.2) precedes head — reused at inference for MC-Dropout (no architecture change needed)
Training: one-epoch frozen warm-up, then end-to-end fine-tuning
NO separate coarse-group head: parent probabilities read directly from 51-label sigmoid outputs
subsections.differentiation_from_asadi2025: Asadi 2025 uses random init (trained from scratch) + adds Conv2D(512)+BN+GAP+Dense(128,ReLU)+Dropout(p=0.5)+sigmoid. We use TXV pretrained backbone with single linear head — simpler head, domain-pretrained weights, no extra conv layers.
subsections.differentiation_from_pham2020: Pham 2020 uses ImageNet pretrained DenseNet-121, 14-dim head, batch=32, 5+5 epochs. We use CXR pretrained TXV weights, 51-dim head, AdamW with differential LRs, cosine annealing with warmup.

subsections.title: Training Objective
key_claims: Flat loss: masked BCE over all 51 findings; NaN → excluded (not counted in numerator or denominator)
Hierarchical loss: HBCE = L_flat + λ × Σ_{(g,c) ∈ edges} penalty(g,c)
λ = 0.5 (same as Asadi 2025 best; no grid search needed for this hyperparameter)
Penalty: zero when predictions are already consistent — does not distort well-calibrated outputs

equations.flat_loss: L_flat = [ Σ_c m_c · BCE(σ(z_c), y_c) ] / [ Σ_c m_c ]   (normalized masked BCE)
equations.hbce_loss: L_HBCE = L_flat + λ · Σ_{(g,c) ∈ edges} penalty(g,c),   λ = 0.5

differentiation_from_asadi2025.asadi_penalty: Penalty(p,c) · 1{p̂_c > 0.5 AND p̂_g < 0.5}   [Asadi Eq.2] — HARD INDICATOR, not differentiable
differentiation_from_asadi2025.our_penalty: ReLU(p_c − 0.5) · ReLU(0.5 − p_g) — DOUBLE-ReLU, fully differentiable everywhere
differentiation_from_asadi2025.key_difference: Our penalty produces a gradient signal proportional to how far p_c exceeds 0.5 and how far p_g falls below 0.5. Asadi's hard indicator gives constant penalty 1 whenever the condition is met — no gradient signal proportional to magnitude.
differentiation_from_asadi2025.cite_sentence: We adapt the hierarchical BCE loss of Asadi et al. (2025) by replacing the non-differentiable indicator function with a product of ReLU activations, yielding a differentiable penalty that varies with prediction confidence.
differentiation_from_asadi2025.beta_adaptation: Asadi also has data-driven β penalty = N_{parent=0,child=1} / N_{parent=0}; we use fixed λ=0.5 for all edges (simpler, same as their best ablation)

optimizer_details.early_stop: patience=3 on validation loss; retain best checkpoint

subsections.writing_note: Specify early stopping clearly: validation loss (not AUROC) is the stopping criterion to avoid optimizing for test-set metric. Best checkpoint by validation loss is what we evaluate.

subsections.title: Uncertainty Estimation
key_claims: Monte Carlo Dropout (Gal & Ghahramani 2016): keep dropout active at inference, T=30 stochastic forward passes
For each finding c: μ_c = (1/T) Σ_t p_c^(t)  (predictive mean)
For each finding c: σ_c = std({p_c^(t)})  (predictive standard deviation)
σ_c is the uncertainty signal used by the gate
No architecture change: same dropout layer (p=0.2) used in training is simply kept active at inference
subsections.differentiation_from_asadi2025: Asadi 2025 uses N=10 MC-Dropout passes and reports uncertainty in the paper, but does NOT use σ_c to gate or route predictions. We use σ_c as an active decision variable at inference.
subsections.differentiation_from_pham2020: Pham 2020 uses NO uncertainty estimation at inference. Their TTA (10 augmentation views) is for accuracy improvement, not uncertainty quantification.

subsections.title: Uncertainty-Gated Coarse Fallback
key_claims: Applied at inference for each IS-A edge (g=parent, c=child)
Three-way decision rule per (g,c) pair
τ_u, τ_p selected on validation set; τ_u = smallest value meeting target hierarchical consistency rate
Parent signal μ_g taken directly from same 51-label sigmoid head — no separate head needed
Gate trades prediction specificity for reliability: smaller τ_u → more fallbacks

equations.rule:
For each IS-A edge (g,c):
  1. if μ_c ≥ τ_p AND σ_c ≤ τ_u: report child finding c
  2. elif μ_g ≥ τ_p: fall back, report parent g (suppress child c)
  3. else: abstain for this (g,c) pair
Findings with no IS-A parent: report if μ_c ≥ τ_p, else abstain.

differentiation_from_pham2020.pham_approach: Hierarchy at TRAINING TIME: exclude parent-negative samples from Phase 1. Bayes product at inference to reconstruct unconditional probabilities. No uncertainty-based routing.
differentiation_from_pham2020.our_approach: Hierarchy at INFERENCE TIME: MC-Dropout variance gate. High σ_c suppresses child and falls back to parent. No training data filtering needed.
differentiation_from_pham2020.key_intuition: Pham 2020: 'train the model to be aware of the hierarchy.' Ours: 'when the model itself is unsure about a child, prefer the more reliable parent.' Complementary philosophies.

differentiation_from_asadi2025.asadi_approach: HBCELoss penalizes hierarchically inconsistent training predictions. At inference: reports μ_c directly, no gating. Uses MC-Dropout for uncertainty but does not route based on it.
differentiation_from_asadi2025.our_approach: At inference: if σ_c > τ_u, actively suppress child and report parent. The MC-Dropout uncertainty determines which level of the hierarchy to commit to.
differentiation_from_asadi2025.key_intuition: Asadi 2025: 'penalize inconsistency during training.' Ours: 'at test time, when uncertain, bet broader.'

subsections.cite_sentence: Unlike Asadi et al. (2025) who use MC-Dropout for uncertainty reporting only, and Pham et al. (2020) who enforce hierarchy during training via data filtering, our gate applies the IS-A hierarchy at inference time: when the predictive standard deviation σ_c exceeds threshold τ_u, the child prediction is suppressed and the model falls back to its parent finding, trading specificity for reliability.

subsections.title: Evaluation Metrics
key_claims: All metrics apply the applicability mask m_c (per dataset)
AUROC: macro and micro over applicable findings per split
F1: macro and micro over applicable findings
ECE: 15 equal-width bins; reliability diagrams for qualitative calibration check
AURC: Zhou et al. (2025) plug-in estimator [Eq.11-12]; coverage = fraction of predictions committed; risk = error rate among committed
AURC comparison: fallback model vs. flat baseline at MATCHED COVERAGE — isolates contribution of coarse fallback step
Coarse prediction correctness: a fallback to parent g counted correct when ANY child c ∈ L(g) is truly positive
Hierarchical consistency: fraction of positive child predictions whose parent is also predicted positive — before and after gate
Grad-CAM: final convolutional block; where bounding boxes available, report pointing-game hit rate and IoU

equations.aurc_formula: AURĈ = (1/n) Σᵢ â_i · ℓ(f(xᵢ),yᵢ),   â_i = Σⱼ₌₁^{rᵢ} 1/(n-j+1)   [Zhou et al. 2025, Eq.11-12]
equations.csf_for_multilabel: g_c(x) = μ_c(x) per label c; system-level CSF = min_c μ_c(x) or per-(image,label) pair independently

subsections.multi_label_aurc_adaptation: Zhou 2025 defines AURC for single-label. We treat each (image, label) pair as an independent selective prediction unit with CSF = μ_c(x). State this adaptation explicitly.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.structural_lesson_source: Pham 2020 §5 (explicit limitations subsection with 7 items); Asadi 2025 (compact but honest)

subsections.title: Key Findings
key_claims: Which factor contributes most: hierarchy loss vs. uncertainty gate vs. segmentation?
AURC improvement: at same coverage, fallback model has lower risk than flat model — clinically meaningful
Hierarchical consistency: gate substantially reduces inconsistent outputs — clinically valid predictions
When the gate fires most: high-σ child findings = Pneumonia subtypes (COVID/Aspiration/Viral) — expected

subsections.title: Limitations
key_claims: Single backbone: DenseNet-121 only; ensemble would likely improve absolute AUROC
IS-A edges manually defined: 13 edges over 51 labels is incomplete; clinical experts should verify
τ_u, τ_p selected on validation: threshold may not generalize to distribution-shifted CXRs
U-Zero for uncertain labels (vs. Pham 2020 LSR): may waste uncertain supervision signal
Single-label AURC adapted to multi-label: per-(image,label) pair treatment is an approximation
No temporal information: sequential CXRs from same patient not exploited
VinDr-PCXR/TBX11K/COVIDx have different label definitions: residual label noise after mapping

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.purpose: Restate problem → contributions → result summary → future work
key_claims: We presented Uncertainty-Gated Coarse Fallback for hierarchical multi-label CXR classification targeting 51 Indonesian canonical findings
Differentiable double-ReLU penalty enables end-to-end hierarchical training
MC-Dropout variance gate at inference time: when uncertain about child, report parent
AURC evaluation shows fallback model achieves lower risk at same coverage vs. flat baseline
8-condition ablation confirms each component contributes independently
Future: extend to deeper hierarchies, Bayesian estimation, multi-view CXR, Indonesian clinical deployment trial
